chunks: Allah, the Exalted, said: “Those who believe, and whose offspring follow them in faith—We shall unite their offspring with them, and We shall not diminish anything from their deeds.”

He said: “Those who believe” are the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, and his offspring are the Imams and the awsiya', may the salawat of Allah be upon them. “We shall unite them with them,” and We did not diminish from their offspring the hujjah which Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله brought concerning 'Ali عليه السلام; their hujjah is one, and obedience to them is one.

key_terms.أَلْحَقْنَا: We joined or united; here referring to linking the offspring with them
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةُ: the Imams, the divinely designated leaders from the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.الْأَوْصِيَاءُ: the successors or legatees appointed after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.الْحُجَّةَ: the divine proof or authority established by Allah
key_terms.بِإِيمَانٍ: in faith; indicating faithful following and spiritual continuity
key_terms.ذُرِّيَّتُهُمْ: their offspring or descendants, understood here as the line of the Imams
key_terms.طَاعَتُهُمْ: their obedience; the obligation to obey them

ai.seo_question: How is Qur'an 52:21 interpreted in Shia hadith regarding the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, and the Imams?
ai.summary: This narration interprets the verse as referring specifically to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, with their offspring identified as the Imams and awsiya'. It emphasizes the continuity and unity of the divine hujjah and the single obligation of obedience owed to them.
